newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan's Bhutto, two aides accused of murder.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan's Bhutto, two aides accused of murder.

text.p: Pakistani police said on Thursday they had received a complaint against former prime minister Benazir Bhutto and two of her aides in connection with two murders committed in December 1995.

They said the complaint, also involving Bhutto's former home minister Nasirullah Babar and former Sindh province chief minister Abdullah Shah, was lodged overnight by a representative of the ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM), a rival to Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party (PPP) in Sindh.
The case was registered at Karachi's Gulberg police station after a complaint made by Shoaib Bukhari, MQM's Labour Minister in the Sindh provincial government, police said.

Police said Bukhari, whose party is now a partner in the Sindh coalition government led by Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's Pakistan Muslim League, accused Bhutto, Babar, Shah and two police officials of responsibility in the killings of Arif Hussain and Nasir Hussain, relatives of MQM chief Altaf Hussain.
There was no immediate information about how the complaint linked responsibility to Bhutto and the others.
A police official said the complaint had been sealed and a senior police official would now follow up the investigation.

Bhutto, whose three-year-old government was dismissed by President Farooq Leghari in November on disputed charges of misrule and whose party was defeated in the February 3 elections, had left for a visit to London on Tuesday.
Her aides were not immediately available for comment on the complaint.
Arif and Nasir were kidnapped from their homes and their bullet-riddled bodies found in the outskirts of Karachi on December 12, 1995, when violence was at its climax in the industrial port city.
More than 2,000 people were killed in ethnic, sectarian and political violence in Karachi in 1995.

Bhutto's estranged brother Murtaza was killed near his home in Karachi on September 20 last year and his breakaway PPP group accuses Bhutto's jailed husband Asif Ali Zardari of conspiring its leader's murder. Zardari denies the charge.
